Summary of the academic seminar on Sukhothai Studies and Lanna Studies, held on 28 March 2018 at the Royal Princess Larn Luang Hotel, Bangkok, with about 130 participants, including Fellows, Associate Fellows, academic committee members, civil servants, academics and the media. The Office of the Royal Society organized the seminar to disseminate knowledge on Sukhothai and Lanna studies and to examine progress and changes over the past decade, and also to pay tribute to Professor Dr. Prasoet na Nakhon, Fellow of the Royal Society in History, Archaeology, a key figure in the academic fields of history, archaeology and literature, on the occasion of his 99th birthday on 21 March 2018

Today (7 Feb 2018), in Meeting Rooms 401–403, the Academy of Science held Meeting No. 3/2018, chaired by Professor Emeritus Dr. Suraphon Itsarakraisin, M.D., Chair of the Academy of Science. The meeting included an Academy of Science dialogue on “How Can Scientists Help the State Reform Thai Education?” and an academic and research lecture by Professor Emeritus Prida Wibunsawat, Fellow of the Royal Society, on “Liberal Arts and Sciences: The Foundation of Higher Education”. A summary of the lecture will be published later

Today (7 Feb 2018), in Meeting Rooms 501–503, the Academy of Moral and Political Sciences held Meeting No. 3/2018, chaired by Professor Dr. Sombun Suksamran, Chair of the Academy of Moral and Political Sciences. The meeting summarized preliminary proposals from the sub-meetings of the working group compiling knowledge for national reform of the Academy of Moral and Political Sciences held on Wednesday, 3 and 17 January 2018. It also considered the Royal Society of Thailand Regulation on Allowances for Fellows and Associate Fellows, B.E. 2561 (2018), and heard an academic and research lecture by Professor Kirati Bunchuea, Fellow of the Royal Society, on “The Philosophy of Good Governance”. A summary of the lecture will be published later

On Thursday, 21 December 2017, at Grand Ballroom 1, Maneechan Resort, Chanthaburi Province, at the 13th seminar on the National Memory of the World Register, Mr. Kritsada Bunyasamit, Associate Fellow, Academy of Moral and Political Sciences, and Chair of the Committee for the Revision and Study of Ancient Thai Law, Office of the Royal Society, proposed registering the Three Seals Law as national documentary heritage and Memory of the World documentary heritage in honor of His Majesty King Buddha Yodfa Chulaloke the Great, with Professor Sawaeng Bunchaloemwiphat as commentator. The Three Seals Law is a compilation of Thai laws from the Ayutthaya period, which King Rama I ordered to be categorized and revised; it has been in use for over 500 years and shows the historical evolution of Thailand in politics, government, economy, society, arts and culture. As the only existing set, it is irreplaceable and therefore important at both national and global levels

Today (1 Mar 2017) at 9:30 a.m., in the 5th-floor meeting room of the Office of the Royal Society, the Academy of Moral and Political Sciences held Meeting No. 5/2017, at which Fellows and Associate Fellows presented their research to the Academy and various important matters were considered. The academic lecture on this occasion was on President Xi Jinping's new political theory under the new normal and strict rule of law, by Mr. Sa-nguan Liumanomon, Associate Fellow. The meeting also elected a new Chair and Secretary of the Academy to replace those whose terms were ending
